newsitem.title: USA: North Dakota farmers to meet USTR Barshefsky.
newsitem.headline: North Dakota farmers to meet USTR Barshefsky.

text.p: U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky will hear complaints from North Dakota farmers about U.S. trade with Canada at a town meeting set for early April, the state's U.S. congressional delegation said Friday.

"As a result of a flaw in the Canadian Free Trade Agreement, our neighbors to the north have had a pattern of flooding U.S. markets with wheat and barley that had a very serious effect on producers in the United States," Sen. Kent Conrad (D-N.D.), said. "Unfair Canadian trade practices have cost North Dakota farmers millions of dollars in lower prices and lost sales."

Sen. Byron Dorgan (D-N.D.) said the free trade agreement between the United States and Canada has hurt U.S. farmers by allowing "an avalanche of unfairly subsidized Canadian grain to come across the border at a time when U.S. farmers were struggling to get higher prices."
The meeting is being sponsored by the state's U.S. congressional delegation comprised of Conrad, Dorgan, and Rep. Earl Pomeroy, a democrat.
It is scheduled to be held in Minot, N.D., on April 2.
